FD vs RD Comparison

An FD vs RD comparison calculator evaluates the return difference between investing a single lump-sum amount in a Fixed Deposit (FD) versus investing periodic monthly installments in a Recurring Deposit (RD) over the same timeframe. Because an FD has all capital compounding from day one, it generates significantly higher total interest than an RD of the same total deposited principal.

--

Formula and Calculation Method

Fixed Deposit compounding formula (compounded quarterly):

FD Maturity = P × (1 + r/4)^(4 × t)

Recurring Deposit quarterly compounding formula:

RD Maturity = Σ [Monthly Deposit × (1 + r/4)^(4 × remaining quarters)]

Worked Example and Step-by-Step Calculation

Comparing $12,000 Total Capital (6.5% APY for 2 Years)
Input Values:
  • FD Strategy: Single $12,000 lump sum at 6.5% for 2 years
  • RD Strategy: $500 monthly deposit ($12,000 total) at 6.5% for 2 years

1. FD Maturity: $12,000 × (1 + 0.065/4)^8 = $13,651.67 (Total Interest: $1,651.67).

2. RD Maturity: Monthly $500 deposits compound to $12,836.42 (Total Interest: $836.42).

3. Difference: FD generates $815.25 more interest because 100% of the funds compound for the full 24 months.

Result: FD Maturity: $13,651.67 vs RD Maturity: $12,836.42 (FD yields +$815.25 more interest)

How to Use the FD vs RD Comparison

  1. Enter the principal amount (either as a lump sum for FD or monthly installment for RD).
  2. Input the annual interest rate offered by your bank or credit union.
  3. Select the tenure in months or years.
  4. Review side-by-side tables showing total invested capital, interest earned, and final maturity.

Common Mistakes, Limitations & Practical Guidance

  • Early withdrawal penalties (typically 0.5% to 1.0% interest reduction) apply if either deposit is broken prior to term maturity.
  • Interest earned is subject to applicable personal income taxes (or TDS) according to your tax bracket.

Frequently Asked Questions About FD vs RD Comparison

What is the main difference between an FD and an RD?

A Fixed Deposit requires a one-time lump sum deposit upfront that earns compound interest for the entire duration. A Recurring Deposit allows you to deposit a fixed installment every month, ideal for savers building wealth from a monthly salary.

Why does an FD yield more interest than an RD for the same total deposit?

In a Fixed Deposit, your entire capital balance is earning compound interest from day one. In an RD, only the first month installment earns interest for the full term, while later installments earn interest for progressively shorter periods.

Are Fixed Deposits and Recurring Deposits insured?

Yes, in the United States, deposits in participating banks are insured up to $250,000 per depositor by the FDIC, and credit union deposits are similarly insured by the NCUA.

Can I choose monthly or quarterly interest payouts?

Yes. Most banks offer cumulative FDs (where interest compounds and is paid at maturity) or non-cumulative FDs (where interest is paid monthly, quarterly, or annually for income).

Which is better for emergency funds: FD or RD?

A high-yield savings account or no-penalty short-term FD is generally better for emergency funds because premature withdrawals from traditional FDs or RDs often incur interest penalties.
